edges.description: Chronic pressure overload is the mechanical stimulus for the cardiomyocyte hypertrophic growth programme, which thickens the ventricular wall to normalise systolic wall stress.
The same pressure overload activates cardiac fibroblasts and TGF-beta/SMAD signalling, driving interstitial and perivascular collagen deposition in parallel with the myocyte hypertrophy.

Mechanical stretch together with the angiotensin II signalling that accompanies pressure overload activates NADPH oxidases, which is the entry point to the oxidative-stress node as that node's own description states.

Sustained arterial pressure injures the coronary microvascular endothelium and drives microvascular rarefaction and perivascular fibrosis, so the workload node also initiates the microvascular arm of the disease.
The thickened, stiffer ventricle relaxes and fills poorly at normal filling pressures, which is why diastolic dysfunction is the earliest functional consequence of the hypertrophic response.

The hypertrophied myocardium has a greater oxygen demand and a reduced capillary density per unit mass, producing a supply-demand mismatch that is worst in the subendocardium even when the epicardial arteries are patent.
Hypertrophied myocardium with altered repolarisation and increased wall stress provides the substrate for atrial and ventricular arrhythmia in this disease.
Myocardial ischaemia is the proximate cause of the anginal chest pain recorded in this entry, which is the reason the phenotype's own note points to underlying coronary artery disease.
Ischaemia impairs the energy-dependent process of active myocardial relaxation and, over time, produces replacement fibrosis, both of which worsen diastolic filling.
Excess interstitial collagen raises passive myocardial stiffness, which is the structural basis for impaired relaxation and elevated filling pressures in this disease.
Patchy interstitial and replacement fibrosis creates zones of slow, non-uniform conduction that support re-entry, adding an arrhythmic substrate distinct from the hypertrophy itself.
Reduced coronary flow reserve limits oxygen delivery to the hypertrophied myocardium during increased demand, producing ischaemia in the absence of epicardial obstruction.
Chest pain without obstructive epicardial disease is the clinical expression of this node, as the phenotype's own note states.
Impaired flow reserve caps the increase in myocardial oxygen delivery achievable on exertion, which the phenotype's note gives as the reason exercise capacity falls.
Reactive oxygen species are one of the two priming and activation signals for the NLRP3 inflammasome named in the downstream node's own description.
Oxidative stress activates the pro-fibrotic signalling this node describes, including NF-kappaB, amplifying collagen deposition beyond what mechanical load alone produces.
Caspase-1-dependent release of IL-1beta and IL-18 amplifies fibroblast activation, one of the two adverse-remodelling outputs this node's description names.
The same inflammatory signalling amplifies the hypertrophic growth response, so inflammasome activation feeds back onto the hypertrophy node rather than acting only downstream of it.
Impaired relaxation raises left atrial and pulmonary venous pressure, especially on exertion, which is the mechanism of breathlessness in hypertensive heart disease before systolic function falls.
A stiff, poorly compliant ventricle decompensates abruptly with small increases in volume or heart rate, which is the basis of the recurrent congestive episodes recorded here.

Limited diastolic filling caps the rise in cardiac output achievable on exertion. This edge records the conventional physiological account; note that the references screened for the Fatigue phenotype in this entry were all graded NO_EVIDENCE for fatigue specifically.
Persistently elevated arterial pressure is the afterload that defines the workload node; without it none of the downstream cardiac remodelling in this entry occurs.

Hypertension accelerates coronary atherosclerotic plaque development and endothelial dysfunction, worsening an ischaemic mechanism that also arises from the hypertrophy and microvascular arms of this entry.

Chronic pressure loading of the aortic wall, with medial degeneration and raised wall stress, is the route from uncontrolled hypertension to intimal tear and dissection. This is extracardiac end-organ damage rather than a consequence of the myocardial chain.

Hypertensive small-vessel disease and large-artery atherosclerosis give both the ischaemic and haemorrhagic routes to stroke recorded in this entry, again independently of the cardiac remodelling chain.
Transmission of systemic pressure to the glomerulus causes nephrosclerosis and glomerular injury, of which proteinuria is the marker recorded here.
BNP is secreted in response to myocardial wall stretch, so the circulating level reports the elevated filling pressures generated by the stiff, poorly relaxing ventricle.
Circulating cardiac troponin reports cardiomyocyte injury, which in this entry is produced by the supply-demand mismatch of the ischaemia node during acute decompensation.

Increased wall thickness with a normal or reduced cavity dimension on echocardiography or cardiac MRI is the imaging readout of the hypertrophy mechanism node, and its concentric geometry identifies pressure overload as the stimulus.

Flow reserve measured by PET or invasively is the functional test result that quantifies the microvascular dysfunction node; the phenotype's own note identifies it as a measurement rather than a structural finding.

nodes.description: First-line agents that reduce workload on the heart.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of hypertensive heart disease with ACE inhibitors.
evidence.snippet: There is evidence to suggest that angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors can play an important role in protecting the heart during the various phases of evolution of hypertensive heart disease both acutely and on a long-term basis.

evidence.reference_title: First-line drugs for hypertension.
evidence.snippet: ACE inhibitors (3 RCTs) reduced mortality (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72-0.95), stroke (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.52-0.82), CHD (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.70-0.94) and CVS (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.67-0.85).

evidence.reference_title: ACE inhibitors and ARBs: Managing potassium and renal function.
evidence.snippet: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) are used primarily to treat hypertension and are also useful for conditions such as heart failure and chronic kidney disease, independent of their effect on blood pressure.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiovascular risk reduction in hypertension: angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers. Where are we up to?
evidence.snippet: Management guidelines categorise angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEI) and angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB) interchangeably as first-line treatments in uncomplicated hypertension.

nodes.description: Lowering blood pressure is the mainstay of treatment to prevent and manage hypertensive heart disease.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanisms and management of hypertensive heart disease: from left ventricular hypertrophy to heart failure.
evidence.snippet: Outcomes in HHD and HF are improved by antihypertensive drugs at any stage of the condition.

evidence.reference_title: Blood Pressure-Lowering Therapy.
evidence.snippet: Extensive evidence demonstrates that lowering blood pressure can substantially reduce the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and death.

evidence.reference_title: Hypertension Treatment in Diabetes: Focus on Heart Failure Prevention.
evidence.snippet: Management of hypertension reduces cardiovascular outcomes among patients with diabetes.

evidence.reference_title: Aortic dissection.
evidence.snippet: Essential treatment includes rapid initiation of pharmacologic agents to control hypertension.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiovascular hypertensive emergencies.
evidence.snippet: In this review, we discuss cardiovascular hypertensive emergencies, including acute coronary syndrome, aortic dissection, congestive heart failure, and sympathomimetic hypertensive crises.

evidence.reference_title: Aortic dissection in children and adolescents with Turner syndrome: risk factors and management recommendations.
evidence.snippet: A clinical profile of those at risk of dissection is emerging and includes the presence of congenital heart defects, aortic dilatation and hypertension.

evidence.reference_title: The Relationship Between Aortic Root Size and Hypertension: An Unsolved Conundrum.
evidence.snippet: Even though arterial hypertension is commonly regarded as a predisposing condition for the development of thoracic aorta aneurysms, the role of blood pressure (BP) as determinant of aortic root enlargement is still controversial.

evidence.reference_title: Chronobiology in aortic diseases - "is this really a random phenomenon?".
evidence.snippet: Similar to other acute cardiovascular events (e.g., acute myocardial infarction, sudden death, stroke, and pulmonary embolism) there is a growing body of evidence regarding temporal patterns in onset, characterized by circadian, seasonal and weekly variations for aortic aneurysms.

evidence.reference_title: Left Heart Disease-Related Pulmonary Hypertension.
evidence.snippet: PH due to LHD is associated with negative impact on outcomes in addition to worse symptoms and exercise capacity.

evidence.reference_title: Cardiac Phenotypes in Secondary Hypertension: JACC State-of-the-Art Review.
evidence.snippet: Evaluation of cardiac phenotypes in secondary hypertension provides a unique opportunity to study underlying hormonal and biochemical mechanisms affecting the heart.

nodes.description: Help control heart rate, reduce oxygen demand, and are especially beneficial after a myocardial infarction.

evidence.reference_title: Beta-blockers in hypertensive and coronary heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Beta-Blockers are widely used in cardiovascular medicine... Based on evidence showing reduced mortality and morbidity, beta-blockers are the cornerstone of therapy after acute myocardial infarction.

evidence.reference_title: Elevated heart rate in cardiovascular diseases: a target for treatment?
evidence.snippet: Today, in patients with acute or chronic coronary syndromes or with congestive heart failure, reducing heart rate is a generally accepted treatment modality.

evidence.reference_title: Heart rate control with adrenergic blockade: clinical outcomes in cardiovascular medicine.
evidence.snippet: One successful way of decreasing HR and cardiovascular mortality has been by utilizing beta-blockers... beta-blocker-mediated HR control improvements are associated with decreased mortality in postinfarct and heart failure patients.

evidence.reference_title: Heart rate recovery improvement in patients following acute myocardial infarction: exercise training, β-blocker therapy or both.
evidence.snippet: Combination of beta-blocker therapy with ET does not compromise the effect of training and instead promotes HRR and aerobic capacity improvement... However, chronic administration of beta-blocker therapy alone did not promote improvement in HRR or aerobic capacity.

evidence.reference_title: Heart disease in the hypertensive patient.
evidence.snippet: Regardless of the level of arterial pressure, vasodilator drugs that lower arterial pressure may result in marked improvement in left ventricular performance and relief of symptoms of left ventricular failure.

evidence.reference_title: Effect of Intensive Blood Pressure Control on Troponin and Natriuretic Peptide Levels: Findings From SPRINT.
evidence.snippet: Given the important role of cardiac injury and neurohormonal activation in the pathways leading from hypertension to heart failure... observed between hypertension and its sequelae on hs-cTnT (high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T) and NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide) levels...

evidence.reference_title: BNP molecular forms and processing by the cardiac serine protease corin.
evidence.snippet: The cardiac hormone, B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP), is one of human natriuretic peptides which possesses cardiorenal protective actions and is used as a therapeutic and a biomarker for heart failure (HF)... circulating NT-proBNP and BNP are elevated in HF...

evidence.reference_title: Practical algorithms for early diagnosis of heart failure and heart stress using NT-proBNP: A clinical consensus statement from the Heart Failure Association of the ESC.
evidence.snippet: Natriuretic peptides (NPs) have been recognized as important biomarkers for diagnosing heart failure... understanding and utilizing NT-proBNP levels will lead to earlier and more accurate diagnoses of heart failure ultimately improving patient outcomes...

evidence.reference_title: Brain natriuretic peptide: diagnostic and therapeutic implications in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
evidence.snippet: Studies in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) have demonstrated that plasma BNP levels are raised proportionally to the extent of right ventricular (RV) dysfunction.

readouts.description: BNP is secreted in response to myocardial wall stretch, so the circulating level reports the elevated filling pressures generated by the stiff, poorly relaxing ventricle.

nodes.description: Chronic pressure overload stimulates fibroblasts to deposit excess collagen in the heart, stiffening it. TGF-β/SMAD signaling drives fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition and increased collagen deposition.

evidence.reference_title: Fibroblasts under pressure: cardiac fibroblast responses to hypertension and antihypertensive therapies.
evidence.snippet: In response to increased peripheral resistance in hypertension, intensified mechanical stretch in the myocardium induces cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and fibroblast activation to withstand increased pressure overload. This changes the structure and function of the heart, leading to pathological cardiac remodeling and eventual progression to heart failure.

evidence.reference_title: Diffuse myocardial fibrosis: mechanisms, diagnosis and therapeutic approaches.
evidence.snippet: Diffuse myocardial fibrosis resulting from the excessive deposition of collagen fibres through the entire myocardium is encountered in a number of chronic cardiac diseases. This lesion results from alterations in the regulation of fibrillary collagen turnover by fibroblasts, facilitating the excessive deposition of type I and type III collagen fibres within the myocardial interstitium and around intramyocardial vessels.

evidence.reference_title: Myocardial collagen remodeling in pressure overload hypertrophy. A case for interstitial heart disease.
evidence.snippet: In left ventricular pressure overload a reactive interstitial fibrosis, having distinctive biochemical and structural features, is seen. This reactive fibrosis occurs in the absence of myocyte necrosis, is progressive in nature, and initially is an adaptive response that preserves the force generating capacity, or active (systolic) stiffness, of the hypertrophied myocardium.

evidence.reference_title: Ischemia and fibrosis: the risk mechanisms of hypertensive heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Mechanisms underlying risk associated with hypertensive heart disease (HHD) and left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) are discussed in this report and provide a rationale for understanding this very common and important cause of death from hypertension and its complications. Emphasized are impaired coronary hemodynamics, endothelial dysfunction, and ventricular fibrosis from increased collagen deposition intramurally and perivascularly.

evidence.reference_title: T helper 17 cell responses induce cardiac hypertrophy and remodeling in essential hypertension.
evidence.snippet: The differentiation of TH17 cells reflected the cardiac hypertrophy and remodeling response to hypertension-induced pressure overload, and it might be a potential inflammatory marker to predict the prognosis of hypertensive patients.

evidence.reference_title: Relationship between hypertension and non-obstructive coronary artery disease in chronic coronary syndrome (the NORIC registry).
evidence.snippet: Hypertension was found in 45% of patients. Hypertensive patients were older, with a higher SIS, calcium score, and prevalence of comorbidities and statin therapy compared to the normotensive (all p<0.05).

evidence.reference_title: A Breathtaking Case of Pulmonary Hypertension with Frightening Complications and Intertwining Different Etiologies.
evidence.snippet: PH is more than a single clinical entity due to its complex mechanism in which more than one subgroup may develop over time in the same patient. This complex mechanism challenges us when diagnosing the patient and faces us with life-threatening complications.

evidence.reference_title: Hypertensive heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is pathognomonic of HHD.

reports_on.description: Increased wall thickness with a normal or reduced cavity dimension on echocardiography or cardiac MRI is the imaging readout of the hypertrophy mechanism node, and its concentric geometry identifies pressure overload as the stimulus.

nodes.description: Hypertension causes endothelial dysfunction, microvascular rarefaction, and perivascular fibrosis in the coronary microvasculature, reducing coronary flow reserve and oxygen delivery to the hypertrophied myocardium. This contributes to ischemia and progression to heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

biological_processes: regulation of nitric oxide biosynthetic process

evidence.reference_title: Endothelial-cell-mediated mechanism of coronary microvascular dysfunction leading to heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
evidence.snippet: Strong evidence has been reported over the past years that coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD), manifesting as structural and functional abnormalities of coronary microvasculature, also contributes to the evolution of HFpEF.

evidence.reference_title: Systemic and Cardiac Microvascular Dysfunction in Hypertension
evidence.snippet: In the context of hypertension, microvascular remodeling and rarefaction result in reduced vessel density and elasticity, increasing vascular resistance and driving end-organ damage.

nodes.description: Reduce fluid overload and congestion in heart failure.

evidence.reference_title: Diuretics: a review and update.
evidence.snippet: Diuretics have been recommended as first-line treatment of hypertension and are also valuable in the management of hypervolemia and electrolyte disorders.

evidence.reference_title: Hypertension and diastolic heart failure.
evidence.snippet: In patients with established heart failure, diuretics and other empiric treatments are used to control symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Newer Drugs to Reduce High Blood Pressure and Mitigate Hypertensive Target Organ Damage.
evidence.snippet: soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators are new classes of chemical agents that... have been shown to be effective for the treatment of cardiovascular (CV) disease (CVD), HF, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D).

evidence.reference_title: Diuretics in States of Volume Overload: Core Curriculum 2022.
evidence.snippet: Diuretics are the cornerstone of therapy for volume overload and comprise several classes whose mechanisms of action, pharmacokinetics, indications, and adverse effects are essential principles of nephrology.

evidence.reference_title: Diuretic Treatment in Patients with Heart Failure: Current Evidence and Future Directions-Part II: Combination Therapy.
evidence.snippet: Fluid retention or congestion is a major cause of symptoms, poor quality of life, and adverse outcome in patients with heart failure (HF)... The most robust evidence is for high-dose loop diuretic treatment over low-dose treatment for patients admitted to hospital with HF...

evidence.reference_title: The Evolution from Hypertension to Heart Failure.
evidence.snippet: Hypertensive heart disease includes the development of diastolic dysfunction, left ventricular hypertrophy, and heart failure with preserved and reduced ejection fraction. The development of heart failure can occur because of complications of ischemic heart disease or from progression of diastolic dysfunction to heart failure with preserved ejection fraction degenerating to a dilated heart with systolic dysfunction or heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

evidence.reference_title: Dyspnea and leg effort during exercise.
evidence.snippet: Dyspnea and leg effort are the major symptoms limiting exercise in healthy subjects and in patients with a variety of respiratory disorders.

evidence.reference_title: Ventilatory Efficiency Is Reduced in People With Hypertension During Exercise.
evidence.snippet: Ventilatory efficiency is impaired people with hypertension without a diagnosis of heart failure versus normotensive individuals.

evidence.reference_title: Exercise Training in Group 2 Pulmonary Hypertension: Which Intensity and What Modality.
evidence.snippet: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) due to left-sided heart disease (LSHD) is a common and disconcerting occurrence. For example, both heart failure (HF) with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF and HFrEF) often lead to PH as a consequence of a chronic elevation in left atrial filling pressure.

evidence.reference_title: Hypertension and diastolic heart failure.
evidence.snippet: Fatigue, dyspnea, reduced exercise tolerance, and peripheral edema are common presenting complaints.

nodes.description: Hypertension increases the pressure the heart must pump against, leading to cardiac remodeling and dysfunction over time.

evidence.reference_title: Large animal models of pressure overload-induced cardiac left ventricular hypertrophy to study remodelling of the human heart with aortic stenosis.
evidence.snippet: Pathologic cardiac hypertrophy is a common consequence of many cardiovascular diseases, including aortic stenosis (AS). AS is known to increase the pressure load of the left ventricle, causing a compensative response of the cardiac muscle, which progressively will lead to dilation and heart failure.

evidence.reference_title: Hypertensive heart disease and heart failure.
evidence.snippet: Hypertension is associated with the remodeling of left ventricular geometry and abnormalities of function that may precede geometric changes. Rather than a specific disease, 'hypertensive heart failure' is a spectrum of disorders that result from left ventricular geometric changes and comorbid conditions.

evidence.reference_title: Diastolic dysfunction as a link between hypertension and heart failure.
evidence.snippet: LVDD as an early measure of myocardial end-organ damage is commonly associated with hypertension and may well precede development of LVH in hypertension.

evidence.reference_title: Increased cardiac work provides a link between systemic hypertension and heart failure.
evidence.snippet: SHR had lower ejection fraction compared with WKY at all ages, but there was no difference in cardiac output at any age. At 21 month the SHR had significantly elevated stroke work (51 +/- 3 mL.mmHg SHR vs. 24 +/- 2 mL.mmHg WKY; n = 8, 4; P < 0.001) and cardiac minute work (14.2 +/- 1.2 L.mmHg/min SHR vs. 6.2 +/- 0.8 L.mmHg/min WKY; n = 8, 4; P < 0.001) compared to control, in addition to significantly larger left ventricular mass to body mass ratio (3.61 +/- 0.15 mg/g SHR vs. 2.11 +/- 0.008 mg/g WKY; n = 8, 6; P < 0.001).

nodes.description: Pressure overload and oxidative stress activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, leading to caspase-1 activation and release of IL-1β and IL-18. This inflammatory signaling amplifies cardiac fibrosis, hypertrophy, and adverse remodeling.

evidence.reference_title: The Role of Inflammasomes in Heart Failure
evidence.snippet: In the pathophysiology of HF, the inflammasome has been correlated with the development, progression, and complications of HF disease.

evidence.reference_title: Diastolic Dysfunction and Hypertension.
evidence.snippet: Hypertension is the most important risk factor for LVDD in the community and promotes LVDD through several mechanisms, including hemodynamic overload and myocardial ischemia.

nodes.description: The heart muscle thickens to cope with increased workload, but this can lead to stiffness and impaired filling.

biological_processes: cardiac muscle hypertrophy in response to stress

evidence.reference_title: Hypertensive heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and diastolic dysfunction (CHF-D) are the early manifestations of cardiovascular target organ damage in patients with arterial hypertension and signify hypertensive heart disease.

nodes.description: Sodium restriction, physical activity, stress reduction, and other supportive measures.

evidence.reference_title: Non-drug treatment of hypertension.
evidence.snippet: These therapies include weight reduction; sodium restriction; potassium, calcium, and magnesium supplementation; other dietary changes; exercise; relaxation; and moderation of alcohol use. Such therapies have been inadequately used, in part because of a lack of confidence in their effectiveness and overconfidence in the effectiveness and safety of drug therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of hypertensive heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Optimal antihypertensive therapy in the setting of therapeutic lifestyle changes is crucial in the prevention and control of HHD.

evidence.reference_title: Impact of therapeutic lifestyle changes in resistant hypertension.
evidence.snippet: Adopting healthy lifestyles, such as being active on >/=4 days per week, weight-loss in the presence of obesity, consuming a diet rich in fruits and vegetables, and sodium below the recommended threshold, avoiding high alcohol consumption and refraining from smoking have been effective lifestyle therapies to prevent or control stage 1 hypertension (HTN).

nodes.description: Further regulate fluid balance and have direct anti-fibrotic effects on the heart.

evidence.reference_title: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists.
evidence.snippet: The vital importance of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists for treating cardiovascular conditions has only been appreciated in the last decade.

evidence.reference_title: Aldosterone and myocardial fibrosis in heart failure.
evidence.snippet: The competitive aldosterone receptor antagonist, spironolactone, was able to prevent fibrosis in both ventricles in either model of arterial hypertension irrespective of the development of left ventricular hypertrophy and hypertension.

evidence.reference_title: Adherence and blood pressure control in patients with primary aldosteronism.
evidence.snippet: All subjects were treated by MR antagonists. 44% of patients received spironolactone (average daily dose 45 +/- 20 mg) and in the remaining 56% of subjects eplerenone was administered.

evidence.reference_title: Aldosterone and volume management in hypertensive heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Aldosterone-receptor antagonists dose-dependently reduce both the epithelial and nonepithelial actions of aldosterone. These compounds are used commonly in the treatment of hypertension, with or without aldosteronism, and in the volume-overload periods of various forms of heart failure, cirrhosis, and renal failure.

evidence.reference_title: Novel Drugs for Hypertension and Heart Failure: Struggling for a Place Under the Sun.
evidence.snippet: Finerenone, a non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist... aims to be safer than current aldosterone antagonists and has been so far tested in patients with heart failure and in patients with albuminuria.

nodes.description: Hypertension can worsen atherosclerosis in the coronary arteries, reducing blood flow to the heart muscle.

evidence.reference_title: Hypertension, coronary artery disease and myocardial ischemic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Hypertension represents a major contributor to the development of coronary artery disease. The pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the link between hypertension and CAD are complex and include overactivation of neurohormones, accelerated development of the atherosclerotic plaque, endothelial dysfunction, altered intramyocardial coronary circulation...

evidence.reference_title: Hypertension and the heart.
evidence.snippet: Sustained increase in arterial pressure causes left ventricular hypertrophy and adversely affects all myocardial compartments: myocytes, interstitium, and coronary vasculature. Ventricular hypertrophy significantly increases the risk for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in hypertensive disease. Impairments in coronary circulation and ventricular fibrosis, which are an essential part of hypertensive disease...

evidence.reference_title: Ischemic Heart Disease Pathophysiology Paradigms Overview: From Plaque Activation to Microvascular Dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: Ischemic heart disease still represents a large burden on individuals and health care resources worldwide. By conventions, it is equated with atherosclerotic plaque due to flow-limiting obstruction in large-medium sized coronary arteries. However, clinical, angiographic and autoptic findings suggest a multifaceted pathophysiology for ischemic heart disease and just some cases are caused by severe or complicated atherosclerotic plaques.

nodes.description: NADPH oxidases (NOX2 and NOX4) generate reactive oxygen species in response to mechanical stress and Ang II signaling. This oxidative stress damages mitochondria, reduces ATP production, and activates pro-fibrotic signaling pathways including NF-κB.

evidence.reference_title: Deciphering Oxidative Stress in Cardiovascular Disease Progression: A Blueprint for Mechanistic Understanding and Therapeutic Innovation
evidence.snippet: This review focuses on the signaling pathways of oxidative stress during the development of CVDs, delving into the molecular regulatory networks underlying oxidative stress in various disease stages, particularly apoptosis, inflammation, fibrosis, and metabolic imbalance.

evidence.reference_title: [Hypertension and the kidney].
evidence.snippet: Hypertension and proteinuria are common risk factors for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, as well as for the progression of renal disease.

evidence.reference_title: Does essential hypertension cause end-stage renal disease?
evidence.snippet: The number of patients developing end-stage renal disease (ESRD) as a consequence of hypertension is increasing and accounts for 25% of new cases of ESRD in the United States. However, the diagnosis of hypertensive ESRD is one of exclusion and no pathologic data corroborate this classification.

evidence.reference_title: Renal damage in hypertension.
evidence.snippet: The kidney can be considered as both culprit and victim in the hypertensive process. Deranged renal function contributes to the development of arterial hypertension and of secondary vascular damage at the glomerular and arteriolar level and accounts for the development of progressive nephrosclerosis.

evidence.reference_title: Spread of glomerular to tubulointerstitial disease with a focus on proteinuria.
evidence.snippet: With ongoing progression and glomerular extracapillary proliferation, tubulointerstitial damage occurs with consequent nephron loss and development of fibrotic lesions, finally resulting in terminal renal failure.

reports_on.description: Flow reserve measured by PET or invasively is the functional test result that quantifies the microvascular dysfunction node; the phenotype's own note identifies it as a measurement rather than a structural finding.

evidence.reference_title: Hypertension and cerebrovascular disease.
evidence.snippet: Hypertension is a leading cause of both stroke and heart disease.

evidence.reference_title: Incidence and risk of stroke in Korean patients with congenital heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Hypertension... for IS only.

evidence.reference_title: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and long-term risk of maternal stroke-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are associated with a long-term risk for... ischemic stroke or hemorrhagic stroke in later life.

evidence.reference_title: Therapeutic Approach to Hypertensive Emergencies: Hemorrhagic Stroke.
evidence.snippet: Arterial hypertension represents the most important risk factor for ischemic and haemorrhagic stroke.

evidence.reference_title: Epidemiology and Primary Prevention of Stroke.
evidence.snippet: Risk factor modification plays a large role in stroke prevention. Strategies for early intervention, particularly for hypertension, are critical for reducing stroke morbidity and mortality.

evidence.reference_title: Visit-to-visit blood pressure variability, silent cerebral injury, and risk of stroke.
evidence.snippet: Apart from the well-known role of hypertension in cerebrovascular disease... an independent risk factor for stroke.

evidence.reference_title: Discerning the relationship between left ventricular geometry, high-sensitivity troponin T, and nondipper hypertension.
evidence.snippet: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) values have been shown to be positively correlated with left ventricular hypertrophy in hypertensive patients.

evidence.reference_title: Longitudinal Changes in Cardiac Troponin and Risk of Heart Failure Among Black Adults.
evidence.snippet: Among Black adults, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) is associated with heart failure (HF) risk. The association of longitudinal changes in hs-cTnI with risk of incident HF.

evidence.reference_title: Biochemical assessment of myocardial fibrosis in hypertensive heart disease.
evidence.snippet: Fibrous tissue accumulation is an integral feature of the adverse structural remodeling of cardiac tissue seen with hypertensive heart disease.

evidence.reference_title: Plasma cardiotrophin-1 levels are associated with hypertensive heart disease: a meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: Increased plasma CT-1 levels are associated with risk for HF in hypertensive patients.

readouts.description: Circulating cardiac troponin reports cardiomyocyte injury, which in this entry is produced by the supply-demand mismatch of the ischaemia node during acute decompensation.

evidence.reference_title: Blood pressure control and left ventricular hypertrophy in hypertensive Nigerians.
evidence.snippet: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) has been shown to be a significant risk factor for adverse outcomes both in patients with hypertension and in the general population.
